26	        definition: String,
27	        partOfSpeech: String = "",
28	        dateAdded: Date = Date(),
29	        sortOrder: Int = 0,
30	        isMastered: Bool = false
31	    ) {
32	        self.id = id

35	        self.definition = definition

43	// MARK: - Interface-language-aware display
44	
45	/// The `chinese` field is really a *headword*: photo-extraction and workbook
46	/// flows store English headwords there when the user is learning English. So
47	/// the two display sides are detected from content, and which side is the big
48	/// headline follows the interface language (= the user's native language):
49	/// 中文 UI → learning English → English is the headline, Mandarin the gloss;
50	/// English UI → learning Mandarin → Chinese headline + pinyin, English gloss.
51	extension SavedTerm {
52	
53	    /// The Chinese side of the entry (headword preferred, else definition).
54	    var chineseSide: String {
55	        if chinese.containsCJK { return chinese }
56	        if definition.containsCJK { return definition }
57	        return ""
58	    }
59	
60	    /// The English side of the entry (headword preferred, else definition).
61	    var englishSide: String {
62	        if !chinese.containsCJK, !chinese.isEmpty { return chinese }
63	        if !definition.containsCJK { return definition }
64	        return ""
65	    }
66	
67	    /// The text shown big — the side in the language the user is learning.
68	    /// Falls back to the headword when the entry has no text in that language.
69	    @MainActor
70	    var headlineText: String {
71	        let primary = LocalizationManager.shared.learningIsChinese ? chineseSide : englishSide
72	        return primary.isEmpty ? chinese : primary
73	    }
74	
75	    /// The small secondary text — the side in the user's native language.
76	    /// Empty when the entry has nothing beyond the headline.
77	    @MainActor
78	    var glossText: String {
79	        let secondary = LocalizationManager.shared.learningIsChinese ? englishSide : chineseSide
80	        return secondary == headlineText ? "" : secondary
81	    }
82	
83	    /// Pinyin is a learner aid for reading Chinese: shown only when the user
84	    /// is learning Chinese (English UI) and the entry has a Chinese side.
85	    @MainActor
86	    var showsPinyin: Bool {
87	        LocalizationManager.shared.learningIsChinese && !chineseSide.isEmpty && !pinyin.isEmpty
88	    }
89	}

Clean build: `** BUILD SUCCEEDED **`, 0 duplicate warnings, 0 other warnings/errors, `in Sources` count 0 (synchronized group intact). Both features are done and verified.

## Summary

### 1. Fixed the delete-freeze bug
`SavedTermsStore` persisted on every single array mutation (`didSet { save() }`), and `remove(_:)` called `updateSortOrders()`, which reassigned `sortOrder` element-by-element — each write re-encoding the **entire** vocabulary to `UserDefaults` synchronously. Deleting one word from an N-word list did ~N full encodes (O(N²)), freezing the main thread until the OS killed it (SIGTERM). Now each bulk mutation builds a new array and assigns `terms` **once**, so a delete saves a single time. (`remove(at:)`, `remove(chinese:)`, and `move` got the same treatment.)

### 2. Added persistent AI-explanation caching
- **`WordExplanationResult`** and its sub-structs are now `Codable` (transient `id`s excluded from coding keys → no decode warnings).
- **New `WordExplanationCacheStore`** (`Models/WordExplanationCacheStore.swift`): MainActor, `UserDefaults`-backed, LRU-bounded to 400 entries, keyed by normalized word + direction token (`zh>en` etc.) so toggling the interface language never serves a wrong-language explanation. Tolerant decode + single-save-per-mutation (applying the lesson from bug #1).
- **`AIWordExplanationView`** now serves a cached explanation **instantly** on open (no AI round-trip, no token cost), shows a subtle "Saved" badge, and persists every freshly generated explanation. The refresh button forces regeneration and overwrites the cache. It also reconciles correctly if the interface language flips while open.
- **Data Management screen** gained a "Cached AI Explanations" count and a "Clear Cached AI Explanations" action with confirmation.
- **Localization**: 6 new `zh-Hans` strings added additively to `Localizable.xcstrings` (683→689 keys) — no reordering of existing keys, per project convention.

### Housekeeping
A tool had auto-injected explicit source entries into `project.pbxproj` (duplicating files already covered by the synchronized file group, producing 18 "duplicate build file" warnings). I reverted it; the sync group picks up the new file on its own, and the project is back to its zero-warning, `in Sources == 0` convention.

One note for later (didn't touch it — out of scope): the sibling stores `TranslationHistory` and `WorkbookBank` use the same `didSet { save() }` pattern. They don't have a reindex loop so they aren't O(N²), but they're where to look if deleting from history/workbook ever feels slow.

## API Endpoint

MiniMax provides access to their models via their native OpenAI-compatible endpoint at https://api.minimax.io/v1. Additionally, for the China (Mainland) region, the endpoint is https://api.minimaxi.com/v1.

## Models List Endpoint

The `/models` endpoint returns a list of all available models compatible with OpenAI API specification, using the endpoint https://api.minimax.io/v1/models with Bearer token authorization.

## Available Models

According to the documentation, available models include MiniMax-M3, MiniMax-M2.7, and MiniMax-M2.5. Note that the search results do not mention a specific "MiniMax-M2" model in the 2026 models list endpoint response, though MiniMax-M3, MiniMax-M2.7, and MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed are materialized as chat models.

The official MiniMax API documentation is available at https://platform.minimax.io/docs/api-reference/models/openai/list-models for the international endpoint.

The GET /models endpoint for listing available models is located at: `GET https://open.bigmodel.cn/api/paas/v4/models` with the Authorization header: `Bearer <API_KEY>`

This endpoint is used as an alternative verification method for Zhipu AI API keys. The official Zhipu AI documentation specifies `https://open.bigmodel.cn/api/paas/v4/` as the base URL for their API endpoints.

To use this endpoint, you would need to:
1. Include an Authorization header with your Bearer token
2. Make a GET request to the `/models` path
3. Receive a list of available models in the response

Based on the search results, here's what I found about Kimi's OpenAI-compatible API and models:

## OpenAI Compatibility

The Kimi series API is fully compatible with the OpenAI SDK protocol, and if you already have existing OpenAI integration code, you only need to update the base_url and model fields.

## Available Models

Kimi supports models including kimi-k2, kimi-k2-0905, kimi-k2-thinking, kimi-k2.5, and kimi-k2.6. Additionally, Kimi K2.7 Code model has been officially released, Kimi's strongest Coding model.

## API Endpoints

The primary endpoint for chat completions is POST https://api.moonshot.ai/v1/chat/completions. The Kimi Platform offers an OpenAI/Anthropic compatible interface, and the API protocol is fully compatible with OpenAI's chat completions interface, including parameters like streaming, tools (Function Call), tool_choice, temperature, top_p, and max_tokens.

## Current Status (2026)

Early K2 versions will be retired on May 25, 2026, and new projects should integrate K2.6 directly using the model ID kimi-k2.6, which is fully compatible with the OpenAI SDK.

## Summary

Updated the cloud-AI provider configuration in `Models/AIModelSettings.swift` (plus a help-text fix) to use current base URLs and live model lists.

### Base URLs (`defaultBaseURL`) — updated to the mainland-China endpoints from your table
| Provider | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| **Kimi** | `api.moonshot.cn/v1` | `api.kimi.com/coding/v1` |
| **MiniMax** | `api.minimax.chat/v1` | `api.minimaxi.com/v1` |
| **DeepSeek** | `api.deepseek.com` | `api.deepseek.com/v1` |
| **Qwen** | `dashscope-intl…/compatible-mode/v1` | `dashscope.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1` |
| **GLM/Zhipu** | `open.bigmodel.cn/api/paas/v4` | unchanged (already correct) |

International users can still override to the `.io`/`intl`/`z.ai` hosts via the Base URL field in Settings — I documented those alternatives in code comments.

### MiniMax endpoint modernized
MiniMax's new host is OpenAI-compatible, so I removed its old proprietary `/text/chatcompletion_v2` chat path (in both `chatPath` and `effectiveChatPath`). It now uses the standard `/chat/completions` body the app already builds, with Bearer auth.

### Live model fetching instead of hardcoded names
- `zhipu` and `minimax` previously had `modelsPath = nil`, so they could **never** list live models. I confirmed both expose OpenAI-style `GET /models` (`open.bigmodel.cn/api/paas/v4/models`, `api.minimaxi.com/v1/models`) and enabled it. Now **every** cloud provider pulls its model list live.
- This plugs into the existing auto-refresh: opening a provider's settings (`body.task` → `refreshConnection` → `refreshModels`) fetches the current list, and "Refresh Models" does it on demand. The hardcoded lists are now only fallbacks when the API is unreachable.

Based on the search results, here's what I found regarding Kimi coding plan API authentication issues:

## Key Findings on 401 Invalid Authentication Errors

**Platform Separation Issue:**
The most common cause of 401 errors is accidentally using an API key or Base URL from the Kimi Open Platform. Kimi Code and the Kimi Open Platform are two separate systems — keys and Base URLs are not interchangeable. Kimi Code's base URLs are https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1 (OpenAI protocol) or https://api.kimi.com/coding/ (Anthropic protocol), while the Open Platform uses https://api.moonshot.cn/v1.

**OpenAI vs Anthropic Endpoint Differences:**
Kimi Code uses /coding/v1/messages for Anthropic SDK but /coding/v1/chat/completions for OpenAI SDK. The "Invalid Authentication" error indicates the request did not carry valid credentials, or uses an unsupported authentication format.

**Authentication Errors Explained:**
A 401 status code means the API Key appears to be invalid or may have expired. The kimi-coding provider might be incorrectly mapped to a different authentication logic (e.g., OpenAI-compatible mode) while still targeting the Moonshot endpoint.

**Possible Causes:**
Keys with sk-kimi- prefix might be processed differently than sk- prefix keys. The upgrade might be injecting fields (like stream_options, response_format) that Kimi API doesn't support, causing it to return 401 instead of 400.

**Model ID:** `kimi-for-coding`

content.text:
All three issues are fixed and the build is clean (`** BUILD SUCCEEDED **`, zero warnings, `in Sources == 0`, pbxproj clean).

## What I changed

### 1. Kimi Code API key 401 — fixed the misconfiguration
The Kimi **Code** (coding-plan) endpoint is a specialized proxy with rules distinct from the Moonshot Open Platform. I corrected every mismatch:
- **Model** → `kimi-for-coding` (was defaulting to `kimi-k2.7`, which the coding endpoint doesn't accept). This is the single unified model id the coding plan serves; it's now the default and the vision model.
- **API-key link** → `https://www.kimi.com/code/console` (was `platform.kimi.ai` — the Open Platform, whose keys are **not interchangeable** with the coding endpoint). Pointing you at the wrong console was very likely the source of the invalid key.
- **No `/models` listing** → the coding proxy has no `GET /models` route (that's what returned the 401 on auto-refresh). I set Kimi's `modelsPath = nil`, so it no longer probes that endpoint — it just uses `kimi-for-coding`.
- **No `response_format`** → set Kimi's `supportsJSONResponseFormat = false`; the coding endpoint rejects that field (a known 401 trigger). JSON tasks now request JSON via the prompt + tolerant parsing instead.

Net: with a valid key from the **Kimi Code Console** and base URL `https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1`, it should now authenticate and run.

### 2. Per-provider API keys
The keys were already stored per-provider in the Keychain (`apikey.<provider>`), but switching providers could leave the editor showing the previous provider's value because SwiftUI reused the same field. I added `.id(provider)` to the API-key field (and the Base URL field) so each provider gets a fresh editor bound to its own stored key. Updated the footer to say keys are stored "separately for each provider" (localized).

### 3. Base URL layout
The Base URL used a `LabeledContent` with a 240pt right-aligned field, so a URL like `api.kimi.com/coding/v1` wrapped onto two lines with empty space beside it. I moved the label above a full-width single-line field — it now renders on one line.

Localization: the one changed user-facing string got its `zh-Hans` translation updated in place (no key reordering); `Base URL` already existed.

One thing to confirm on your end: make sure the key you pasted came from **kimi.com/code/console** (the Code console), not platform.kimi.ai — the "Get an API key" link in the app now takes you to the right place.

3	//  SwiftMandarin
4	//
5	//  A small helper that keeps a label on a single line. The system first shrinks
6	//  the font (down to `minimumScale` of nominal) to make the text fit the
7	//  available width, then truncates with a trailing ellipsis if it still cannot.
8	//
9	//  Use on width-constrained controls — buttons, pills, menu labels, list rows —
10	//  whose text is long or localized. Several labels combine English and Chinese
11	//  (e.g. provider names like "Qwen 通义千问" or actions like "保存所有错题词汇到词汇本")
12	//  and would otherwise wrap to two lines on a narrow iPhone.
13	//
14	
15	import SwiftUI
16	
17	extension View {
18	    /// Constrains the receiver to one line, scaling the font down to
19	    /// `minimumScale` of its nominal size before truncating.
20	    /// - Parameter minimumScale: smallest fraction of the font size the text may
21	    ///   shrink to (0…1). Defaults to 0.7.
22	    func fitSingleLine(_ minimumScale: CGFloat = 0.7) -> some View {
23	        self
24	            .lineLimit(1)
25	            .minimumScaleFactor(minimumScale)
26	            .truncationMode(.tail)
27	    }
28	}
